references.title: Geogram: a programming library of geometric algorithms

filters.name: Mesh Union (geogram)
filters.shortDescription: Create the exact union of two mesh layers using geogram.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Computes the exact boolean union of two mesh layers and creates the result as a new layer, using geogram's exact predicates. Both operands should be closed, consistently oriented surfaces without self-intersections; *Repair Self-Intersections (geogram)* can prepare an input that is not.

parameters.label: First Mesh
parameters.help: First operand of the boolean operation.

parameters.label: Second Mesh
parameters.help: Second operand of the boolean operation.

parameters.label: Simplify coplanar facets
parameters.help: Merge facets that end up coplanar in the result. Turning this off keeps every triangle the intersection produced, which is larger but preserves the original tessellation more closely.

filters.name: Mesh Symmetric Difference (geogram)
filters.shortDescription: Create the exact symmetric difference of two mesh layers using geogram.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Computes the exact boolean symmetric difference (XOR) of two mesh layers and creates the result as a new layer.

geogram's boolean evaluator provides union, intersection and the two differences, but not the symmetric difference, so this filter composes it as $(A \setminus B) \cup (B \setminus A)$. That is **three** boolean evaluations rather than one, so expect it to take roughly three times as long as *Mesh Difference (geogram)* on the same operands. Both operands should be closed, consistently oriented surfaces without self-intersections; *Repair Self-Intersections (geogram)* can prepare an input that is not.

parameters.label: First Mesh
parameters.help: First operand of the boolean operation.

parameters.label: Second Mesh
parameters.help: Second operand of the boolean operation.

parameters.label: Simplify coplanar facets
parameters.help: Merge facets that end up coplanar in the result. Turning this off keeps every triangle the intersection produced, which is larger but preserves the original tessellation more closely.

filters.name: Repair Self-Intersections (geogram)
filters.shortDescription: Remove self-intersecting faces and retriangulate the holes using geogram.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Attempts to make a surface conformal by removing intersecting faces and retriangulating the holes they leave, using geogram's exact predicates. The result is created as a new layer.

The pass is repeated until no intersection remains or the iteration limit is reached, so a mesh with deeply nested intersections may need more than the default number of iterations. This is the usual way to prepare an input for the geogram boolean filters, which require operands without self-intersections.

parameters.label: Maximum Iterations
parameters.help: How many times to repeat the remove-and-retriangulate pass before giving up.

filters.name: Parametrize by Least Squares Conformal Maps (geogram)
filters.shortDescription: Compute a Least Squares Conformal Maps UV parametrization using geogram.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Computes a Least Squares Conformal Maps parametrization of the current mesh and stores the result as per-vertex texture coordinates. LSCM minimizes conformal (angle) distortion with two fixed points, so the mesh must have a boundary. If the mesh already carries per-wedge texture coordinates they are synchronized from the new per-vertex ones, so the result is immediately visible in the texture and UV views.

This is the reference implementation, by the authors of the original paper.

The flattening follows the mesh's existing vertex connectivity: coincident but distinct vertices stay split and appear as a seam, so run *Remove Duplicate Vertices* first on a mesh loaded from a format that does not share them, such as STL.

filters.name: Parametrize by Angle-Based Flattening (geogram)
filters.shortDescription: Compute an ABF++ angle-based UV parametrization using geogram.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Computes an ABF++ (Angle-Based Flattening) parametrization of the current mesh and stores the result as per-vertex texture coordinates. ABF++ solves for the flattened *angles* rather than the vertex positions, which generally yields noticeably lower angle distortion than LSCM on the same input, at a higher cost. The mesh must have a boundary. If the mesh already carries per-wedge texture coordinates they are synchronized from the new per-vertex ones.

This is the reference implementation, by the authors of the original paper.

The flattening follows the mesh's existing vertex connectivity: coincident but distinct vertices stay split and appear as a seam, so run *Remove Duplicate Vertices* first on a mesh loaded from a format that does not share them, such as STL.

filters.name: Parametrize by Atlas (geogram)
filters.shortDescription: Segment the mesh into charts, flatten each one and pack them into a single atlas, using geogram.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Runs geogram's complete atlas pipeline on the current mesh: the surface is cut into charts along sharp edges, each chart is flattened, any chart whose distortion is still too high is split further, and the charts are finally packed into the unit square. The result is stored as per-wedge texture coordinates.

Unlike the single-chart flatteners, this works on a **closed** mesh, because the segmentation step creates the boundaries the flatteners need.

If the mesh already carries a `chart` face attribute the pipeline uses it to seed the segmentation.

parameters.label: Hard Angle Threshold
parameters.help: Edges whose dihedral angle exceeds this value, in degrees, become chart boundaries. Lower values cut the surface into more, flatter charts.

parameters.label: Chart Parametrizer
parameters.help: How each individual chart is flattened.

enumOptions.label: Least-Squares Plane Projection
enumOptions.help: Project onto the best-fitting plane. Fastest, and only reasonable for charts that are already nearly flat.

enumOptions.label: Least Squares Conformal Maps
enumOptions.help: Conformal flattening with two fixed points.

enumOptions.label: Angle-Based Flattening
enumOptions.help: ABF++, the lowest distortion of the three and the default.

parameters.label: Chart Packer
parameters.help: How the flattened charts are arranged in the unit square.

enumOptions.label: None
enumOptions.help: Leave each chart where its flattening put it; charts will overlap.

enumOptions.label: Tetris
enumOptions.help: The packer from the original LSCM paper.

enumOptions.label: xatlas
enumOptions.help: geogram's bundled copy of xatlas. MeshLab also ships xatlas directly as Parametrize by Atlas (xatlas).

filters.name: Pack UV Charts (geogram)
filters.shortDescription: Lay the existing UV charts out again in a single atlas, using geogram's packers.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Rearranges the charts of an existing parametrization in the unit square, leaving the flattening of each chart untouched. The mesh must already carry per-wedge texture coordinates.

The Tetris packer is the one described in the original LSCM paper and is not available from any other MeshLab filter.

parameters.label: Packer
parameters.help: Which packing algorithm to apply.

enumOptions.label: Normalize Charts Only
enumOptions.help: Do not pack; only rescale each chart so its texture area is proportional to its area on the surface.

enumOptions.label: Tetris
enumOptions.help: The packer from the original LSCM paper.

filters.name: Compute Chart Segmentation (geogram)
filters.shortDescription: Partition the mesh into charts and store each face's chart index in the face scalar field.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Segments the current mesh into a requested number of charts and stores the chart index of each face in the per-face scalar field, so the partition can be shown with the scalar colormap and used by later filters. No texture coordinates are created.

The two VSA segmenters implement Variational Shape Approximation: the $L^2$ metric groups faces by position and the $L^{2,1}$ metric by normal, which makes the latter follow anisotropic features more closely.

parameters.label: Segmenter
parameters.help: Which segmentation algorithm to use.

enumOptions.label: Variational Shape Approximation (L2)
enumOptions.help: Continuous VSA with the L2 metric; groups faces by position.

enumOptions.label: Variational Shape Approximation (L2,1)
enumOptions.help: Anisotropic VSA with the L2,1 metric; groups faces by normal.

enumOptions.label: Shortest Inertia Axis
enumOptions.help: Split into two segments along the shortest inertia axis. Ignores the requested chart count.

parameters.label: Chart Count
parameters.help: How many charts to aim for. The segmenter may return a different number.

filters.name: Remesh by Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation (geogram)
filters.shortDescription: Rebuild the surface from a centroidal Voronoi tessellation, isotropically or aligned to curvature.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Rebuilds the current mesh by distributing the requested number of vertices over the surface with Lloyd relaxation followed by Newton optimization, then extracting the restricted Voronoi diagram as the new tessellation.

In **anisotropic** mode the optimization runs in a six-dimensional space where the extra three coordinates are the surface normal scaled by the anisotropy strength, so elements stretch along flat directions and concentrate across curved ones. No other remesher in MeshLab offers this; the isotropic mode competes with *Remesh Isotropically (vcglib)* and *(TrueForm)*.

The vertex count is a target, not a guarantee: geogram may add vertices to resolve problematic configurations. Because the surface is rebuilt from scratch there is no correspondence with the original tessellation, so **per-vertex and per-face attributes are not preserved** — transfer them back afterwards with a filter from the Transfer family.

parameters.label: Target Vertex Count
parameters.help: How many vertices the result should have. geogram may exceed it to resolve problematic configurations.

parameters.label: Anisotropic
parameters.help: Align elements with the surface's curvature instead of keeping them as equilateral as possible.

parameters.label: Anisotropy Strength
parameters.help: How strongly elements follow curvature, as a fraction of the bounding box diagonal. Larger values stretch them more. Ignored unless Anisotropic is set.

parameters.label: Adjust to Source Surface
parameters.help: After remeshing, nudge the vertices so the new faces approximate the original surface more closely.

parameters.label: Adjust Search Distance
parameters.help: How far to search for the nearest original vertex, relative to the local average edge length. Ignored unless Adjust to Source Surface is set.

parameters.label: Lloyd Iterations
parameters.help: Lloyd relaxation passes, which spread the vertices out evenly before the Newton phase refines them.

parameters.label: Newton Iterations
parameters.help: Newton optimization passes. More gives a better-conditioned tessellation at a higher cost.

parameters.label: Newton Hessian Samples
parameters.help: How many evaluations the Newton solver uses to approximate the Hessian.
